question.text: Vatsalya Charitable Society, a NPO whose ZCZPs are listed on BSE-SSE, suffers the sudden departure of its Chief Program Officer - a key managerial personnel. Under Regulation 91(D) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015, within what time must the NPO disclose this event to the SSE?

answer.text: As soon as reasonably possible but not later than 7 days from the occurrence of the event.
Within 3 working days as per Regulation 30 of LODR.
Within 24 hours of the board meeting where the departure is noted.
Within 30 days along with the next quarterly utilisation statement.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 91(D)(4) of LODR provides that disclosure of a material event to SSE shall be made 'as soon as reasonably possible but not later than seven days from the occurrence of the event.' This is the SSE-specific timeline; Reg 30 (main-board) 24-hour / 30-minute timelines do NOT apply to SSE filings. The Trap: 3 working days / 24 hours / 30 minutes are Regulation 30 timelines for main-board equity issuers - candidates often reflex to those because they appear in III-A/III-C. The SSE regime under 91(D) is a separate sub-code with its own 7-day rule. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C Compliance tests Reg 30 timelines for main-board issuers; XXIII tests the SSE-specific 7-day rule under 91(D)(4). Mixing the two is the most common MCQ trap in this area. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Include a 'materiality watch-list' in the SIA engagement file: KMP turnover, revocation of 12AB or FCRA, regulator show-cause, programme-site inaccessibility. The SIA won't file the 91(D) intimation (the SE's KMP will), but during AIR fieldwork the SIA verifies each event was disclosed in 7 days and tags unfiled items as a material weakness.
